(i) women's groups have a greater likelihood of success in achieving their policy goals if the Commonwealth government acts alone or in cooperation (but not in competition) with sub-national governments; and (ii) women's groups are more likely to be successful in achieving their aims if they have access to decision-making structures and are able to participate in the policy process.
